summary: Bounded primary-author witness search for issue #345 following the degree fork/core investigation. The canonical 2022-01-23 post is readable now, but normal source-tool fetches have different HTML byte hashes because of per-request Cloudflare r/t script parameters. Extracted post text is stable; rejected stripping/normalizing those nonce bytes or pinning an inevitably drifting HTML response. Found the actual author-advertised /4/feed RSS anchor after a blank rel=alternate link. Four normal source-tool fetches of https://robkoons.net/4/feed were byte-identical; pinned the verbatim UTF-8 XML using the existing web_snapshot/raw_text variant, without adding any extractor or source kind. Materialized KOONS-FOURTH-WAY-RECONSTRUCTION-2022-FULL-ITEM, then read the complete uniquely identified content:encoded item, all thirteen numbered steps and both closing paragraphs. The truncated description and search snippets were not the witness. Canonical human citation, feed URL/hash, exact item title/date/GUID and access failures are preserved in the source/passage records and docs/notes/koons-fourth-way-reconstruction-2022-reading.md. The returned interpretation distinguishes possible-maximum and imported modal/causal blocks from the existing strict nonmodal profile; no attributed claim, Lean formalization, root-premise substitution or unconditional branch elimination is added. The issue paraphrase is not accepted as source evidence. Failed Wayback/CDX/availability probes and zero Arquivo.pt capture results are documented; no fixed capture is invented. The primary feed avoids the observed HTML volatility but remains fragile against future updates without a fixed archive fallback. A bibliographic_span is neither needed nor created. One coherent comparison candidate retains the next semantic question. Source integrity does not settle source fidelity or formal consequence; actual root-premise delta is none. Validation at source checkpoint 7aba445b78225b151b33ed4d584517cdc589a7d8: source_evidence.py check and corpus.py check passed; normal source_evidence.py verify --base HEAD^ --head HEAD refetched and verified exactly the one newly pinned RSS passage (61854f98b488), with all other passages checked offline only. Source text was not taken from a cached search rendering. Integrity follow-up after main revision 73dcbb13, run 40747604144 job 123026416902 failed at 18:53:52 UTC with HTTP 404 from the pinned /4/feed URL: the exact historical bytes remain in the ignored source cache. Fresh production-header downloads and a cache-disabled materialize_web_snapshot verification on 2026-10-28 returned all 54,102 original bytes and the unchanged byte/text SHA256 61854f98b4887ae9c5cbdea88f9fd1a83a4f1a318a0412dc6e058629ee1d9047. The live endpoint recovered; no hashes, locators, license, claims or interpretation were changed. The www and HTTP publisher variants also returned the same bytes; /old-blog-2021-22/feed returned a different feed hash and was rejected as an exact-byte replacement. Wayback CDX returned an empty capture list and its availability API reported no archived snapshots; Save Page Now timed out, so no durable fallback is claimed. The CI 404 remains a transient availability failure, not evidence of source drift. No premise change; no full workflow was cancelled or repeated. See the linked reading note for the focused reproduction command and remaining fragility. Independent hosted-CI recovery evidence supplied by the coordinator: integrated main a13fc469, run 40749570362, corpus-and-lean job 123032417241 passed including full source verification with unchanged witness inputs. No retry of the old failed main workflow and no source-change PR is needed.
